chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Miskin, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Najjah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'The obligatory prayer overtakes me, or its time enters, so I begin with the voluntary prayer.' He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but begin with the obligatory prayer and complete the voluntary prayer.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order of prayer when time is short: obligatory or voluntary?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural priority of fard (obligatory) prayers over nafl (voluntary) ones when time is constrained, ensuring the fulfillment of the primary duty before supplementary acts. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the completion of the wajib prayer takes precedence, even if it means performing the nafl prayer later as a make-up (qada) rather than in its ideal sequence. This ruling underscores the importance of not delaying the core obligation due to the desire for additional voluntary worship.
